# A5 — Can you predict, on day one, which postings close within 14 days?

*Spec frozen 2026-10-20 (panel day 44), before any final-test posting exists. Generated by
`python -m analysis.a5_prediction`; the final run needs the panel through 2026-11-30. The numbers
below come from `--interim`, a pipeline check, and are in `report/a5_results_interim.json`.
**They are not the result.***

## Why this is in the report

The plan is explicit: A5 is less about building a supervised model than about how it is
evaluated. So the design below is fixed before the test data exists, and the headline will be
whatever the frozen ladder says, including "gradient boosting adds nothing".

## Design (frozen)

| | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Population | Postings we saw **born**: first seen after panel day 1, within 1 day of the employer's publish date | "Day one" has to really be the posting's first day. Postings already live on 2026-09-07 have unknown day-one state |
| Label | **Closed within 14 days of first sighting** (final disappearance, as in A2) | The plan's question |
| Not a close | A closure that A7 classifies as a **repost**. The role carried on under a new ID | A2/A7 showed these inflate fast closures |
| No label (dropped) | The employer's whole board vanished within the 14 days (e.g. Postman) | We can't know what would have happened |
| Labelled when | The panel has watched the posting for the full 14 days | Otherwise a recent posting looks "still open" by construction |
| Features | Family, seniority, city, workplace, company (≥ 5 training postings, else `other`), skills per 5, log description words, log number of the employer's live postings that day, relisted (same employer and title seen on an earlier day), multi-country | All knowable on the posting's first day. Description length uses raw text, because boilerplate removal is learned from the whole corpus, future included |
| **Primary split** | **Train: first seen ≤ 2026-11-01 (weeks 1–8). Test: first seen after.** | The plan's 8/4 temporal split. Postings from weeks 11–12 can't get 14 days of follow-up, so the test set is in effect weeks 9–10 |
| Secondary | **Rolling origin**: refit at each week's end from 2026-09-27 on all earlier postings, predict the next week, pool | Roughly triples the test positives; the cost is that predictions from different models are pooled |
| Ladder | 1 majority (training base rate) → 2 single best feature, chosen by 5-fold CV ROC AUC **on training only** → 3 logistic regression (L2, C = 1) → 4 gradient boosting (depth 3, learning rate 0.05, 200 iterations, ≥ 10 per leaf) | The plan's ladder |
| Tuning | **None.** Hyperparameters fixed above | ~40 training positives is too few to tune without tuning to noise |
| Diagnostic | Logistic without `company` | Is the signal just the employer? |
| Metrics | ROC AUC, **PR AUC** (≈ 16% positive), Brier. 95% CIs from 2,000 bootstrap resamples stratified by outcome; lift of each rung as a **paired** bootstrap CI | The plan's metrics; paired, because all rungs are scored on the same postings |
| Calibration | Quantile-binned reliability curve (5 bins), mean predicted vs observed rate, calibration slope | The plan's calibration check |
| Interpretation | Permutation importance on the test set (ROC AUC drop, 50 repeats) | Association, not cause |

## Power, stated in advance

Born postings arrive at about 4.7 a day, and about 16% close within 14 days. Projected final
numbers: **train ≈ 260 postings / ≈ 40 positives; test ≈ 70 / ≈ 10–12.** With 9 test positives,
the interim run's ROC AUC intervals are about ±0.14 wide. The final test set will be no better, so
**the primary split can only resolve lifts of roughly 0.25 AUC or more.** A gap of a few points
between logistic regression and boosting will be reported as unresolved. It won't be declared a
win in either direction. The rolling-origin pool (projected ≈ 230 postings / ≈ 35 positives)
narrows this to about ±0.08, and that is why it's there.

## Interim pipeline check (2026-10-20)

Train weeks 1–3 (91 postings, 13 positives), test 2026-09-28 → 10-06 (51 postings, 9 positives).

| Rung | ROC AUC (95% CI) | PR AUC (95% CI) | Brier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Majority | 0.50 | 0.18 | 0.146 |
| Single feature (`company`) | 0.55 (0.40–0.71) | 0.24 (0.17–0.35) | 0.141 |
| Logistic | 0.84 (0.70–0.97) | 0.67 (0.44–0.90) | 0.110 |
| Gradient boosting | 0.72 (0.53–0.89) | 0.31 (0.23–0.56) | 0.157 |
| Logistic without company | 0.85 (0.69–0.98) | 0.73 (0.48–0.94) | 0.099 |

The pipeline runs end to end, but the interim numbers shouldn't be read as performance. **The
logistic lift is mostly one employer.** Six of the nine test positives are Twilio and Airbnb
postings with no Indian city and remote work. Several of them were seen only once or twice before
vanishing. Both companies have fewer than 5 training postings, so they fall into `other`, and the
model picks them up through `city = no_city` and `workplace = remote`, which act as a proxy for
the employer. That's why dropping `company` costs nothing. It's the report's recurring theme again
(the employer explains more than the role does), now as a leakage-style trap. In the final run,
with ~8 weeks of training, both employers clear the 5-posting threshold, and the `company` term
should absorb this.

Boosting loses to logistic regression here (PR AUC −0.36, paired CI −0.55 to −0.06), as expected
on 91 rows. The logistic model is well calibrated in the large (predicted 0.18 vs observed 0.18).

## What would change my mind

- **If the final logistic model clears the single best feature by less than the CI width**, the
  honest summary is "on day one, the employer's identity is about as good as anything". That would
  fit A2, where role family didn't predict closure either.
- **If the lift survives in the rolling-origin pool but not the primary split**, the primary is
  underpowered, not wrong. Report both, and lead with the primary, as frozen.
- **If permutation importance puts `city` or `workplace` above `company` again in the final run**,
  the employer proxy isn't absorbed, and the model is still mostly identifying employers.

## Limitations

1. Small: ≈ 10 primary test positives. See *Power*.
2. "Closed" means it vanished from the ATS, not that it was filled. Repost closures are handled,
   other non-fill closures are not.
3. Only born postings are used, about 40% of everything seen, and skewed to the employers that
   posted during the panel.
